facts.text: Founded in 1786 by Irish immigrant William Dunn, Dunnstown—originally Dunnsburgh—stands as the oldest regularly plotted community in the West Branch Valley.
The West Branch Canal reached Dunnstown in 1833, sparking a brief lumber and navigation boom before Irish laborers and German boatmen clashed in August of that year.
After the canal closed, the 1881 paper plant—later part of the Lock Haven Paper Company—became Dunnstown’s largest employer until the industry’s decline in the 1970s.
The 1950s GI Bill housing boom produced ranch‑style homes along Reeds Run, a feature that still defines Dunnstown’s residential character today.
Dunnstown’s historic dam and the nearby Great Island—a 325‑acre alluvial plot once used by Munsee Delaware villages—highlight the area’s rich pre‑colonial and canal‑era heritage.
William Dunn’s grave in the Dunnstown Cemetery marks the original settlement site, keeping the town’s namesake alive for visitors and locals alike.
